subject: Hyperscaler performance claims — proposed challenge plan & econ tests
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@edgescale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo — inference economics and hyperscaler comparison

Elaine — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and the three concrete asks we agreed to: 

1) What you heard from the hyperscaler: lower per-token cost for bulk batch workloads (their published numbers assume batch sizes >=64, aggressive prefix caching, and model vX.2).
2) What we heard from EdgeScale: procurement needs a clear per-1M token comparison, security wants SOC2 evidence, and ops wants a short, automated benchmark to validate latency at your P95 SLA.

Proposed next steps (we can start once you grant a short-lived data token / test corpus):
- Challenge plan: run side-by-side inference runs across the same model family (we'll use the open 7B variant you called out) on three configs: Redwood-hosted (managed runtime), Hyperscaler standard endpoint, and a Hyperscaler optimized endpoint (if they provide one).
- Tests: (A) Per-1M token cost at batch sizes [1, 16, 64], (B) Cache hit sweep: simulated prefix cache hit rates [0%, 50%, 90%], (C) Latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99) with token-limited sequences (256 / 1024).
- Deliverables: CSV of raw samples + cost calc workbook, short executive summary (1 page) with recommended production config and estimated unit economics.

I attached the call recording and a short initial proposal. If that all looks right, can you confirm: 1) dataset share (S3 presigned or drive link), 2) budget guardrail for the pilot (approx $1k–$5k), and 3) preferred date for the technical cleanup call next week?

Thanks — I’ll triage this internally and have Marissa/Connor scope the experiments.

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Hyperscaler performance claims — EdgeScale pilot plan

Team — forwarding EdgeScale ask. High priority: procurement wants per-1M token ballpark and security wants SOC2 evidence. Proposed internal test matrix (please comment inline in the attached benchmark-plan.xlsx):

Test matrix (goal: apples-to-apples economics + latency):
- Model: open-7B-qa (float16 quantized where supported) — same weights across runs.
- Platforms: Redwood-hosted (managed), Hyperscaler A (public endpoint), Hyperscaler A optimized tier (if available).
- Workloads: 5k-sample corpus, tokenized to avg 120 tokens/sample.
- Batch sweep: batch sizes [1, 16, 64].
- Cache/sparsity sweep: simulated prefix hits at [0%, 50%, 90%] by replaying common prefixes from corpus.
- Metrics: cost per 1M tokens (USD), GPU-hours, P50/P95 latency, failure rate, tokens/sec throughput, cache-hit effective reduction in token compute.
- Success criteria: show <20% delta in cost per 1M tokens vs hyperscaler at production batch profile OR provide explicit operational tradeoffs (e.g., latency uplift but 30% cost savings).

Ops notes: Connor — can you slot 8h on Friday to provision benchmark infra and make sure the runtime picks quantized kernels? Marissa — can you draft the short per-1M token ballpark so procurement has a number to work with by Wed EOD? Neha — please attach SOC2 evidence and the short data handling checklist to the Drive folder.

Link to plan: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_plan (see benchmark-plan.xlsx).

Thanks — Ben

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@edgescale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@edgescale.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Hyperscaler performance claims — proposed challenge plan & econ tests

Elaine / Marta — looping back with the concrete plan and timeline. Attached is the benchmark-plan.xlsx (short matrix) and a 1-page econ summary (ballpark per-1M token estimates under typical product traffic). Key points up front: 

- Ballpark per-1M tokens (expected ranges): Redwood-hosted: $32–$45 per 1M tokens depending on batch; Hyperscaler (public): $28–$40 per 1M tokens (their numbers assume large batches and high cache reuse). We’ll produce precise measured numbers after the runs.
- Proposed pilot timeline: benchmark runs next Tue/Wed (Dec 8–9); quick internal analysis on Dec 10; delivery of report and exec 1-pager by Dec 11.
- Data exchange: please share the presigned S3 link (or Drive) and confirm we can store results in a shared folder for 30 days.
- Next call: suggest Dec 12, 11:00 PT for a 30–45m review where we walk the numbers and suggested production configs.

Attachments/links: benchmark-plan.xlsx, call recording, initial-proposal-edgescale.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf (in Drive).

If that timeline works I’ll confirm infra scheduling with Connor and Marissa. One ask for transparency: if EdgeScale hears any concrete instance-level pricing/offering from the hyperscaler (SKU names, commit discounts, or reserved instance assumptions) that materially change unit economics, please forward — it helps us match apples-to-apples in the comparison.

Looking forward —
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
(Attachment: benchmark-plan.xlsx)
